title: Practical Fundamentals of Astrophysics
summary: A 4-week, quantitative introduction to astrophysics tailored for self-learners, covering radiation physics, stellar mechanics, stellar life cycles, and introductory cosmology with daily bite-sized calculation tasks.

days.title: Cosmic Distances and Coordinate Systems
objectives: Convert between astronomical units, parsecs, and light-years
Calculate stellar distances given parallax angles in milliarcseconds

days.title: Blackbody Radiation and Stellar Temperatures
objectives: Calculate peak emission wavelengths using Wien's displacement law
Determine total radiant surface flux using the Stefan-Boltzmann law

days.title: Flux, Luminosity, and the Inverse-Square Law
objectives: Calculate radiant flux received at Earth given a star's luminosity and distance
Estimate stellar radii using luminosity and effective temperature

days.title: The Magnitude Scale and Distance Modulus
objectives: Convert between radiant flux ratios and apparent magnitude differences
Calculate source distances using absolute magnitude and the distance modulus equation

days.title: Stellar Spectroscopy and Spectral Classification
objectives: Identify stellar spectral classes (OBAFGKM) based on characteristic absorption lines
Determine surface temperatures and compositions from absorption line profiles

days.title: Keplerian Orbits and Binary Mass Determination
objectives: Calculate combined system masses from orbital periods and semi-major axes using Kepler's third law
Estimate individual masses of stars in spectroscopic binary systems

days.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium in Stars
objectives: Calculate central pressure estimates of stars using the hydrostatic equilibrium equation
Explain why a star maintains a stable size against gravitational collapse

days.title: Core Nuclear Fusion and Energy Generation
objectives: Calculate mass-energy conversion efficiency for the proton-proton chain
Compare conditions required for the proton-proton chain versus the CNO cycle

days.title: The Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram and Stellar Groups
objectives: Plot stars on an H-R diagram using luminosity, color index, and temperature
Distinguish main-sequence stars, giants, and white dwarfs by their positions on the H-R diagram

days.title: Mass-Luminosity Relations and Main-Sequence Lifetimes
objectives: Calculate luminosity from stellar mass using empirical power-law relations
Estimate the main-sequence lifetime of a star relative to the Sun

weeks.theme: Stellar Evolution, Remnants, and the Interstellar Medium

days.title: The Interstellar Medium and the Jeans Instability
objectives: Calculate the Jeans mass and Jeans length for a cold molecular cloud
Determine whether an interstellar cloud core will undergo gravitational collapse

days.title: Post-Main-Sequence Evolution of Low-Mass Stars
objectives: Trace the evolutionary path of a Sun-like star through the red giant and asymptotic giant branches
Describe the physical mechanism forming a planetary nebula and white dwarf

days.title: Degeneracy Pressure and the Chandrasekhar Limit
objectives: Explain electron degeneracy pressure using the Pauli exclusion principle
Calculate the radius and density of a carbon-oxygen white dwarf near the Chandrasekhar mass

days.title: Core-Collapse Supernovae and Neutron Stars
objectives: Calculate the gravitational binding energy released during a core collapse
Estimate neutron star densities and surface gravitational acceleration

days.title: Stellar-Mass Black Holes and the Event Horizon
objectives: Calculate the Schwarzschild radius for a given stellar mass
Compute the gravitational redshift for photons emitted near an event horizon

days.title: Galactic Structure and Rotation Curves
objectives: Calculate orbital speeds of disk stars as a function of radius
Infer the presence and distribution of dark matter from flat galactic rotation curves

days.title: The Extragalactic Distance Ladder
objectives: Estimate distances to nearby galaxies using Cepheid period-luminosity relations
Use Type Ia supernova peak magnitudes as standard candles to measure cosmological distances

days.title: Hubble-Lemaître Law and Cosmic Expansion
objectives: Calculate recessional velocities from observed cosmological redshifts
Estimate the expansion age of the universe using the Hubble constant

days.title: The Cosmic Microwave Background
objectives: Calculate the temperature of the early universe at decoupling using CMB redshift
Explain the physical origin of CMB blackbody radiation and its temperature fluctuations

days.title: Cosmological Parameters and the Universal Energy Budget
objectives: Calculate the critical density of the universe given the current Hubble constant
Estimate the relative contributions of baryonic matter, dark matter, and dark energy from density parameters
